_comment: wp_appliance — PASSIVE edge/VPN appliance fingerprint -> CISA KEV mapping -> patch-lag inference (techniques/fx-edge-appliance-recon.md). Every endpoint, product pattern, advisory row, port-risk row and caveat lives here (RULE 3) so a renamed CPE, a new KEV product string or a new vendor advisory is a data edit, not a code change. Nothing here is case data: public vendor names, public CPE vocabulary and public PSIRT/KEV dates only. The tool never contacts the target: it reads Shodan InternetDB (keyless), Shodan host and Censys host (keyed, metered — skipped under free_only / scope no_spend) and the public KEV catalogue.

settings._comment: internetdb_url / shodan_host_url take {ip}; the Shodan key is appended by the caller and never logged. kev_url = CISA's public KEV JSON feed; kev_cache_path is relative to the engine root (intel_engine/) unless absolute — the default cache/ dir is gitignored. kev_ttl_hours = re-download when the cache is older than this; a stale cache is still used (status stale_cache, with the reason) when the refresh fails. max_ips caps how many A records of one domain are looked up. max_kev_per_product caps the family list. snmp_wrap_days = 2^32 TimeTicks / 100 / 86400 (RFC 2578 §7.1.8); tcp_ts_wrap_days = a 1 kHz TCP-timestamp clock. wrap_alternatives = how many wrapped readings to list beside the face value. boot_window_days = the +/- on every boot estimate. confirmed_version_bases = the version bases that count as a CONFIRMED version for the CRITICAL escalation. Owner decision: ONLY `analyst` (the analyst verified the version and passed --version-confirmed / version_confirmed=true). A version read from a CPE (cpe_version), the index's own product/version field (index_version_field), a banner pattern or a build string is index-announced, can be stale or spoofed, and stays TENTATIVE.
settings._comment_metered: METERED pre-filter (Shodan host = 1 query credit, Censys host = 1 credit of the 100-a-month free quota). The keyless InternetDB leg runs first for every IP; a metered leg is bought only for an IP whose InternetDB record shows a catalogue CPE (products.*.cpe), a port in metered_gate_ports (the VPN / admin / IKE ports edge appliances listen on) or a tag in metered_gate_tags; InternetDB not_found or an unrelated record buys nothing. max_metered_ips caps how many IPs of one run get the metered legs (max_ips still caps the keyless leg). The planned credit count is computed before any spend and reported in metered_plan.

products._comment: Product catalogue from the technique doc's fingerprint table, plus common peers. cpe = [{vendor, product}] regexes matched (case-insensitive, search) against the vendor/product fields of a CPE 2.2 (cpe:/a:v:p:ver) or 2.3 (cpe:2.3:a:v:p:ver) string. banner = regexes over the index's stored banner text, HTTP title, headers and body — product evidence only. version_regex = optional regexes with ONE group that read a version out of that stored text (basis banner_regex, never confirmed). build_map = announced build string -> version (Fox-IT style tables); empty means a build stays UNMAPPED. kev = regexes matched against the KEV entry's vendorProject and product (the FAMILY match). fingerprint_paths are documentation for an AUTHORISED direct check only; this tool never requests them.

editions._comment: Citrix ships standard, FIPS and NDcPP firmware trains that share the release numbering (13.1-37.x exists as a standard build AND as FIPS builds), and the vendor documents NO build range that separates them. Two vendor-documented passive signals only: (1) markers — Citrix names FIPS firmware with 'FIPS' in the version ('14.1-FIPS, build 72.61', NetScaler FIPS FAQ; the bulletins name '13.1-FIPS' / '12.1-NDcPP'); a marker counts only inside version-bearing evidence (a CPE string, the index's product/version field, a version_regex hit), never anywhere in a page body. (2) standard_builds — exact standard build numbers per branch from the vendor's standard release-notes index; an exact match identifies a STANDARD build. Absence from the list is NOT evidence of FIPS (the index is not exhaustive, e.g. 13.1-49.13 is missing). Anything else is edition-unknown: when an advisory's per-edition fixed lists disagree on it, it stays TENTATIVE with the reason.

build_regex._comment: Cache-busting build strings on login-page static assets, read from the index's STORED HTTP body (never fetched). One group = the build. A build is UNMAPPED unless the product's build_map names it.

advisories._comment: Vendor PSIRT rows for well-known KEV CVEs, each checked on 2026-11-15 against the vendor's own advisory (source_url) and the vendor-authored CVE record; KEV dateAdded / dueDate come from the live CISA catalogue at run time, not from here. wp_appliance IGNORES any row without both `verified` and `source_url` (an analyst's --advisory is exempt — it is the analyst's own claim). fixed_in lists the first fixed release per branch as the vendor states it (the STANDARD edition where editions exist); branch_depth = how many leading version numbers define a branch (2 = 13.1 / 7.4; 3 = PAN-OS hotfix trains like 10.2.8). A branch the vendor lists as affected with no fix (EOL) is absent from fixed_in, so it reads branch_unlisted — except in an edition-aware row, where affected_no_fix names those standard branches. fixed_fips / fixed_ndcpp (Citrix only) = the same bulletin's FIPS / NDcPP fixed releases, verified from the same source_url; their presence turns on edition-aware comparison (products.<pid>.editions decides the edition; an unknown edition whose per-edition verdicts disagree reads ambiguous_edition). An edition list left empty ([]) means not confirmed from the vendor and never yields a definite verdict. fixed_in null = no per-branch list kept here (Cisco / Exchange: left empty on purpose) — version status stays unknown and only the lag after the advisory is reported. upgrade_reboots is null everywhere: no vendor upgrade note was checked, so the uptime rows never assert that a fix needs a reboot. Removed on verification (no primary source for the advisory date): CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 (Ivanti — the KB article and blog did not expose the original publication date).
advisories._comment_version_status: branch_only means the observed version names the same branch as the fixed release but has fewer numeric components (13.1 vs 13.1-49.15). Compare only versions at least as specific as the fix. branch_only never asserts pre-fix status, never computes lag or past_kev_due, never yields CRITICAL, and never writes a kev_exposure KB fact. kev_exposure is written only for pre-fix KEV matches; other family matches remain in the scan output only.

CVE-2023-4966.notes: fixed_in = standard builds; fixed_fips / fixed_ndcpp = the bulletin's 13.1-FIPS, 12.1-FIPS and 12.1-NDcPP fixes (same source_url). Standard 12.1 is EOL and affected with no fix (affected_no_fix).

CVE-2023-3519.notes: fixed_in = standard builds; fixed_fips / fixed_ndcpp = the bulletin's 13.1-FIPS, 12.1-FIPS and 12.1-NDcPP fixes (same source_url). Standard 12.1 is EOL and affected with no fix (affected_no_fix).

CVE-2019-19781.notes: CTX267027 itself no longer resolves; Citrix's CTX267679 states it was released on 2019-12-17.

CVE-2022-1388.notes: 12.1.x and 11.6.x are affected with no fix (branch_unlisted). The K-article is script-rendered; date and versions read from F5's own CVE record, which cites K23605346.

CVE-2023-46747.notes: Fixed by engineering hotfixes per branch, not a plain release number — no fixed_in kept. Date from F5's own CVE record, which cites K000137353.

CVE-2022-42475.notes: FortiOS 5.x is affected with no fix (migrate) — branch_unlisted.

port_risk._comment: Exposed-service port-risk matrix from the technique doc (passive, from the index's port list). critical=true marks container/cluster control planes that should never face the internet (hand off to techniques/cloud-audit.md).

uptime_fields._comment: Where an index record stores an uptime, read from each Shodan service record. path = dotted path in the record; unit = minutes | seconds | timeticks (1/100 s); clock = snmp_sysuptime (32-bit TimeTicks, wraps every snmp_wrap_days) | tcp_timestamp (wraps every tcp_ts_wrap_days at 1 kHz) | unknown (both wrap caveats are stated).

caveats._comment: Wording the output attaches. The tool never writes the words that claim exploitability; it reports lag and reboot evidence only.

entries.general: Passive scan-database evidence only — the target was not contacted. A fingerprint confirms the product, not exploitability; the version-to-CVE mapping stays TENTATIVE until the version is verified (/vuln-check, vendor advisory, authorised check).
entries.kev_family: KEV entries are matched on the product FAMILY (KEV vendorProject + product). A family match says this product line has known-exploited CVEs; whether this device's version is affected depends on the version.
entries.index_vulns: Index CVE lists (InternetDB / Shodan `vulns`) are inferred by the index from the announced version; they are not verified.
entries.snmp_wrap: Counter wraparound: SNMP sysUpTime is 32-bit TimeTicks (1/100 s) and wraps every ~497.1 days (RFC 2578 §7.1.8), so the face value may be the uptime plus a multiple of 497.1 days. Corroborate with two scans far apart: the uptime must grow by the elapsed time.
entries.tcp_wrap: A TCP-timestamp uptime (1 kHz clock) wraps every ~49.7 days, and many OSes randomise the TCP-timestamp offset per connection (RFC 7323), so such a value is often meaningless.
entries.ha_pair: Load balancers and HA pairs: one IP can front several nodes; the uptime belongs to whichever node answered that scan.
entries.hot_patch: Hot patching: some fixes, mitigations or live-patches apply without a reboot; a long uptime shows only that no reboot-requiring update was applied.
entries.clock_offset: The index timestamp may be ingest time rather than probe time, and a scanner may cache an earlier uptime; the boot date is 'on or about' (at least +/-1 day).
entries.ha_conflict: Conflicting uptimes across records of this IP point to an HA pair or load balancer, not to a reboot.
entries.lag_wording: Lag is the days between the vendor advisory and the latest index record still announcing a pre-fix version. It is not a statement that the device is exploitable or compromised.
entries.kev_due: Past the KEV due date is prioritisation context (BOD 22-01 binds US federal agencies), not a legal finding about a non-federal subject.
